decisions.reason: As a recent extension of the core radiant-heating line, it likely meets at least a provisional aspiration level and, in a growing firm with slack, is worth retaining while market feedback accumulates.

The electric infrared panel heater fits the firm's move toward lower-carbon building-climate solutions, and with only a short market history there is no strong signal of underperformance that would justify exit.

Because it was actively marketed and broadens the firm's electric infrared offering, management would likely tolerate early uncertainty and keep it unless clearer evidence of results below aspiration emerged.
This product is close to the established offer and serves the firm's industrial hall customer base directly, so the expected fit and low adaptation burden support keeping it on the market.

The hydrogen-capable heater matches the firm's strategic direction and was already placed in real operation, so despite uncertainty management would likely continue it as an important option for future demand.
